subject: Renewal: commit sizing options, uplift guardrails and per-token ladder
messages:

Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal coming up — questions on commit tiers and per-token ladder

Hi Irene,

Hope you had a good holiday break. Our renewal for Redwood is up in mid-February and procurement wants clarification on how your per-token discounts and commit tiers work for hosted API usage. Two specific asks from our finance team:

- We want to understand the practical delta between a 12-month 1.5B token commit vs 2.0B (how often do we hit the next tier historically?).
- What are the allowable uplift limits at renewal (our headcount could increase ~20% next year and they want guardrails on surprise charges).

Also: are there true-up windows or quarterly smoothing options? If you can share a couple of concrete commit scenarios with price ladders and an example true-up calculation, that would be super helpful.

Thanks — Amira

Sentinel Health

Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — questions on commit tiers and per-token ladder

Hi Amira — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Ben (sales) and Laura (finance) so you get a concise proposal and the accounting perspective. High-level thoughts below and I attached three modeled scenarios.

Quick answers:
- Historical uplift behavior: for orgs your size we see ~10–18% year-over-year token growth on average; margin depends heavily on burst patterns and KV cache effectiveness.
- Uplift guardrails: we support capped uplift ranges (customer-defined) and a one-time smoothing true-up per year; we can also apply quarterly true-up windows for larger accounts.

Attached is a spreadsheet (redwood_commit_scenarios.xlsx) that shows three options:
A) Conservative: 1.25B commit — per-token base $0.0008, 5% at 1.5B, 10% at 1.75B
B) Balanced: 1.6B commit — base $0.00075, 7% at 1.9B, 12% at 2.25B (recommended if you expect steady growth)
C) Aggressive: 2.2B commit — base $0.00070, 10% at 2.6B, 15% at 3.0B

We typically set an annual uplift cap (e.g., 15%) to prevent surprise overages; you can choose quarterly true-ups with proportional smoothing. If you prefer, we can add a clause limiting billing increases to X% year-over-year (with a true-up reconciliation).

Questions for you:
- Does procurement need a firm maximum uplift % in the contract or is a smoothing mechanism enough?
- Do you want committed spend expressed as tokens or a dollar committed minimum (we can do either; tokens align best to usage economics).

Ben/Laura — can you confirm the discount ladder we can reasonably offer for a 1.6B commit (Sentinel is at negotiation stage, would like a slightly stronger anchor).

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — questions on commit tiers and per-token ladder

Amira — appreciate the context. Based on usage patterns we observed last 12 months, here is a counter-proposal tuned to reduce Sentinel's downside while giving them predictable unit economics:

Offer summary (Balanced anchor with optional protection):
- 12-month commit: 1.6B tokens 
- Effective per-token rate: $0.00072 (first 1.6B)
- Overage rate: $0.00090 per token (or apply 60% of the committed rate beyond a one-time capped uplift)
- Discount ladder: at 1.9B drop to $0.00068, at 2.4B drop to $0.00064
- Renewal uplift cap: 15% absolute increase in billed spend year-over-year unless mutually agreed otherwise
- Quarterly smoothing: true-up applied at quarter end, with a single annual settlement to limit billing volatility

Attachment: price_sheet_v3.csv (contains modelled effective rates)

If Sentinel wants a contractual hard cap on monthly billing increase, we can set a monthly band (e.g., +/-25% smoothing) and then reconcile annually. That typically satisfies procurement and finance audit teams.

Happy to jump on a quick call next week to walk through the scenarios.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Amira,

From a finance perspective we prefer:
- Commit expressed as tokens (cleaner for unit economics).
- Renewal uplift cap: 15% max unless there is a signed amendment. We can carve out a one-time exception for major acquisitions or M&A with 30 days' notice.
- True-up: quarterly smoothing with annual reconciliation (helps monthly P&L).
- True-up window: 30 days after quarter close to submit usage questions.

Also attaching the statement-of-work draft and proposed billing terms — SOW_SENTINEL_v2.pdf. We can shorten payment terms from Net45 to Net30 if Sentinel signs for the Balanced scenario (1.6B).

Let us know if procurement needs an explicit clause: "Annual billed spend may not increase by more than 15% over previous 12 months except by signed amendment." We can add that as an appendix.

Thanks,
